issues.legal_issue: Conviction for rioting or constructive liability based on membership in an unlawful assembly requires certainty that at least five persons shared its common object.
material_facts: Six people were charged as the only members of the alleged unlawful assembly.
Two of the six were acquitted, leaving fewer than five people established as members of the assembly.
The charge alleged that the assembly shared the object of demolishing a thatch and attacking anyone who resisted.
issues.conclusion: The convictions for rioting and for offenses based on unlawful-assembly liability could not stand because the charge named only six alleged members and two were acquitted, so the court could not find with certainty that at least five people shared the common object.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 141 and 149 of the Indian Penal Code require an unlawful assembly of at least five persons, and constructive liability under section 149 cannot be applied unless the court finds with certainty that at least five persons shared the common object. It is not invariably necessary to convict five people: where five were unquestionably present but the identity of one or more is uncertain, the others may still be convicted. Section 148 likewise depends on the existence of an unlawful assembly. The Court relied on Dalip Singh v. State of Punjab, Mohan Singh v. State of Punjab, and Krishna Govind Patil v. State of Maharashtra.

predicates.unlawful_assembly_prosecution: The proceeding seeks conviction for an offense that depends on the accused being members of an unlawful assembly.
predicates.only_named_members_include_acquitted_peo: The charge identifies a limited group as the only members of the alleged assembly, and some members of that group are acquitted.
predicates.fewer_than_five_members_are_certainly_es: The evidence and findings do not establish with certainty that at least five people shared the alleged common object.
predicates.conviction_based_on_unlawful_assembly_me: A conviction that depends on unlawful-assembly membership is set aside.

issues.definition: When an unlawful-assembly prosecution identifies a limited group as its only members, some are acquitted, and fewer than five are certainly established as sharing the common object, the membership-based conviction cannot stand.

issues.legal_issue: Participants may be convicted for offenses committed in furtherance of their common intention when a prior concerted plan is established from the circumstances, even if unlawful-assembly liability cannot be sustained.
material_facts: The remaining accused arrived together, armed, to pull down the thatch after a dispute and a threat that it should be removed.
When people resisted, the accused attacked them with weapons, causing severe injuries and the deaths of two people.
The evidence showed coordinated conduct during the attack, and the accused left the scene together.
The Court inferred a preconcerted plan to remove the thatch and to attack anyone who resisted.
issues.conclusion: The remaining accused were guilty of culpable homicide not amounting to murder and attempted murder under common-intention liability; those convictions replaced the convictions based on unlawful-assembly liability.
issues.legal_principle: Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code applies where a criminal act is done by several persons in furtherance of their common intention. Common intention is distinct from the common object of an unlawful assembly and requires action in concert and a plan that precedes the act constituting the offense. The plan may develop at the scene, but it must exist before the relevant act. Common intention may be inferred from the totality of circumstances, including how the accused arrived and attacked, the coordinated nature of the injuries, assistance by other participants, and their conduct after the offense. The Court relied on Dalip Singh v. State of Punjab, Mohan Singh v. State of Punjab, and Krishna Govind Patil v. State of Maharashtra.

predicates.criminal_case_involving_joint_participat: The proceeding concerns offenses allegedly committed through the joint participation of multiple accused.
predicates.group_arrived_together_armed_to_carry_ou: The accused arrived together, armed, to carry out a shared objective.
predicates.participants_attacked_people_who_resiste: The accused attacked people who resisted their shared objective.
predicates.coordinated_conduct_supports_a_prior_pla: The manner of arrival, conduct during the attack, assistance among participants, or conduct afterward supports an inference that a common plan existed before the relevant criminal acts.
predicates.remaining_participants_are_convictable_f: The remaining participants may be convicted for offenses committed in furtherance of their common intention.

issues.definition: When jointly participating accused arrive armed to carry out a shared objective, attack those who resist, and their coordinated conduct supports a prior plan, the remaining participants may be convicted for offenses committed in furtherance of their common intention.
